messages:
incident-bot: INC-2026-045: SmartRouting errors increasing across eu-west-1 -> us-east-1. 5xx up 7x over baseline in last 3m. Paging @arjun (on-call) :rotating_light:

arjun: on it. @maya assign priority 1. grabbing graph and routing logs.

maya: seeing surge starting 12:33 UTC, looks correlated with a forced model pin in eu-west-1. metrics: latency + request errors up, customer 502/503s.

emily: logs snippet from router at 12:34:12:
```
RouteDecision[req=abc123]: prefer=eu-west-1 -> candidate=rwind-v2-quant (unavailable) -> fallback=us-east-1 -> candidate=rwind-v1-legacy (available) -> route->us-east-1
RouteDecision[req=abc124]: prefer=us-east-1 -> candidate=rwind-v1-legacy -> fallback=eu-west-1 -> candidate=rwind-v2-quant (forced_pin) -> reject -> fallback->us-east-1
// loop detected: fallback bounce count=6
```

liam: fyi that was my manual change. earlier today we forced the enterprise account to rwind-v1-legacy in eu-west-1 to avoid a perf regression on their workload. i used the force-pin CLI and forgot to add ttl. my bad. command i ran:
```
redwoodctl routing set-variant --scope=eu-west-1 --model=rwind --variant=rwind-v1-legacy --force
```

maya: that explains forced_pin true on many requests. thanks for flagging. are we currently pinned at a global/policy level or region scope?

liam: thought region-scoped, but checking now... giving output:
```
Applied variant override: scope=global, target=eu-west-1, variant=rwind-v1-legacy, ttl=0
```

olivia: oof global scope + ttl=0 == permanent until manually removed. that will make routers reject newer variant availability and trigger fallback cycles.

emily: fallback loops look like this: routers try eu-west -> forced var missing capacity -> fallback to us-east -> us-east returns candidate but then routing policy tries prefer eu-west due to higher priority -> bounce -> kv-cache invalidations spike -> cache miss + double KV reads -> downstream 503s.

samir: CS reporting multiple customers seeing degraded responses, some timed out, escalations inbound. tilly can you paste CS thread?

tilly: https://company.slack.com/archives/customer-ops/p12345 -> customer says ~20% requests failing since 12:35 UTC, started complaining at 12:40.

arjun: mitigation plan (short): 1) remove force-pin immediately, 2) temporarily disable cross-region fallback policy, 3) scale eu-west serving to absorb legacy variant if needed, 4) clear router KV cache to stop stale decisions. I'll handoff to emily to execute.

emily: taking it. executing step 1 now.

emily: running
```
redwoodctl routing unset-variant --scope=global --target=eu-west-1 --model=rwind
```

deploy-bot: command accepted, change id=chg-2026-778, applying to routing-config.

liam: i'm going to disable fallback routing temporarily while we stabilize:
```
redwoodctl routing update-policy --name=cross-region-fallback --enabled=false --reason="incident-1825554321 emergency"
```

deploy-bot: policy update applied chg-2026-779.

olivia: heads-up - when removing the override please ensure no residual policy pins exist. earlier someone used `--scope=global` by accident and it propagated. verify via `redwoodctl routing list-overrides`.

liam: i ran list-overrides and it now shows none for rwind. verifying global state... okay clear.

emily: clearing KV caches on routers in eu-west-1:
```
kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deployment/router-eu-west-1
kubectl -n redwood exec router-pod-12 -- redis-cli FLUSHALL
```

emily: restarting router pods. monitoring error rate.

~2m later~
maya: error rate dropping from 7x to 1.3x, latency returning to baseline for most customers. some legacy sessions still failing due to session-affinity sticky routing to pods that were restarted.

samir: CS confirms fewer complaints, but a few enterprise customers still seeing intermittent 503s. stacking notes for post-incident.

arjun: quick note: during the revert liam accidentally applied a change to the global routing policy because he omitted `--scope=region`. that toggled the policy to prefer legacy variants everywhere for a minute; thanks to disabling fallback we avoided a bigger blast but that was a close one.

liam: facepalm emoji. i see it: command history shows `--scope=global` in my earlier command. will open a PR to add a safeguard flag.

olivia: we should add a guard in the CLI to require `--force` + confirmation if scope=global, or require ttl for force-pin. file a ticket.

emily: i'm handing this to on-call night shift (emily -> emily? i'm staying) but arjun, if you need to fully take over for postmortem, ping me. i'll stay to watch for 20 more minutes then hand to emily_night if needed.

arjun: handing off to emily for mitigation and monitoring. Handoff notes:
- changed: removed global override for rwind, disabled cross-region fallback policy, restarted routers in eu-west-1, flushed KV cache
- impact: transient 5xx spike 12:33-12:45 UTC, partial customer impact, CS escalations ongoing
- action items: liam to file CLI guard PR, ops to add automatic TTL on manual force-pin, eng-platform to add dry-run checks before scope=global applied

emily: acknowledged. will keep monitoring and post resolution update.

~15m later~

emily: all quiet. error rates at baseline, no new customer complaints in last 10m. re-enabling fallback policy only after we add stricter variant availability checks.

deploy-bot: re-enable request queued chg-2026-790 by emily.

emily: re-enable with stricter checks = `--min-available-replicas=3 --reject-if-variant-unavailable=true` applied.

maya: good call. schedule follow-up postmortem tomorrow, include network/routing logs, CLI audit, and CS timeline.

samir: assigning postmortem owner: liam (author) + eng-platform (assignee). Samir will triage customer impact.

tilly: CS follow-up message drafted to affected customers, waiting on final validation.

arjun: incident declared resolved at 12:50 UTC. Good work all. add retro item: restrict manual global overrides to a small admin group and add TTL enforcement.

emily: closing monitoring loop. next steps: create incident doc and link here.

deploy-bot: incident INC-2026-045 status=resolved changelog=[chg-2026-778,chg-2026-779,chg-2026-790]
